groups.title: Cylinder Gases
groups.summary: Cylinder gases in every size, refilled and delivered from a network of fill plants.
groups.intro: AWG delivers thousands of cylinders each week through a company owned fleet of more than 250 route trucks and vehicles. An infrastructure of fill plants inside the distribution network keeps product on hand for day to day use and for spikes in demand. The full range of cylinder sizes is stocked, and staff help pick the size that fits the job.

Several supply sources behind each gas, to reduce the risk of running short
Quality checked through AWG laboratories and production plants in Indianapolis, IN and Beaumont, TX

groups.title: Bulk Gas Systems
groups.summary: Bulk tanks engineered, installed, monitored by telemetry and refilled before they run low.
groups.intro: AWG application engineers and bulk technicians design the bulk supply system, handle the installation and the permits, and leave room for the site to grow. Telemetry sensors on the tank report pressure or liquid level back to AWG, so stock is watched and reordered before it runs down. A multi-site supply chain and supplier partnerships keep product moving through regional and national shortages.

groups.title: Specialty and Medical Gases
groups.summary: High purity gases, calibration standards, medical grades and beverage carbon dioxide.
groups.intro: AWG Specialty Gas is an independent producer of high purity gases and mixtures for laboratory, manufacturing, research and environmental work. Its two manufacturing sites, in Indianapolis, Indiana and Beaumont, Texas, are accredited to ISO/IEC 17025:2017 and ISO 17034:2016, and the company also runs an ISO 17025 laboratory in Lexington, KY. Medical and beverage grades are packaged in cylinders or supplied as bulk liquid.

groups.title: Welding and Cutting Equipment
groups.summary: Welding machines, plasma and oxy/fuel cutting outfits, and the apparatus that feeds them gas.
groups.intro: AWG carries welding and cutting machines and accessories from the major manufacturers, for the hobbyist bench and for industrial production alike. Oxy/fuel outfits need no electricity, travel easily and change over to welding or brazing tips; plasma cutters drive an arc through a jet of ionised gas to cut conductive metal quickly and cleanly. Gas apparatus is put together as a custom system, from one cylinder feeding one welder up to bulk storage serving several points.

about.title: A gas and welding supply house with roots in 1949
text: American Welding & Gas is a family and teammate owned company headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina. It traces its history to Valley Welders Supply in Billings, Montana and the Scott-Gross Company in Lexington, Kentucky, both founded in 1949, and has grown since then both organically and by acquisition.

Today AWG runs more than 100 retail locations and 22 gas fill plants across 22 states, from Montana to Pennsylvania and south through Texas and Florida, with more than 800 employees serving customers in over 30 states and Canada. A fleet of more than 250 trucks and trailers carries the product: palletized cylinder delivery trucks, cryogenic tankers and tube trailers.

The line runs from bulk cryogenic gases to packaged cylinders, taking in industrial, medical, specialty and beverage gases alongside welding and safety supplies. The Baytown store on West Main Street is one of those locations.
